note: Martin County's largest park, on Cedar Lake north of Trimont, with a swimming beach, boat launch and fishing piers. Camping is paid in cash or by check in the envelopes at the park on arrival. --Claude
summary: County pages read: $25 electric / $15 primitive / $450 a month confirmed (fees unchanged), first-come with a 7-day limit, 37 water+electric sites (amps not stated), flush + pit toilets, showers, dump, closed for the season (no dates). Pin is in the lake: move ~280 m to Google's point. Not waterfront kept (sites under canopy, no site map). Phone none -> 507-236-4693 (park caretaker). Google 4.2/23.
flags: PIN: stored 43.79450,-94.73560 is in Cedar Lake, about 50 m off the north shore. Move to Google's point 43.79220,-94.73418 (about 280 m SSE), in the wooded park area beside the farm buildings north of the peninsula. The campsites themselves are under full canopy and cannot be placed on imagery.

Waterfront: keep not waterfront. The park has 'approximately one mile of shoreline' and a wooded peninsula, but no site map was found and imagery shows only canopy over the camping area, so no site can be placed within 50 m of the lake. Unverified either way; downgrade rule keeps it down.

Monthly sites: the fees page lists 'Monthly Camp Sites $450 per month' and the FAQ 'Seasonal camping sites are available for $450/month', while the rules say 'A campsite cannot be occupied for longer than 7 consecutive days by the same party.' The share of monthly sites is not published. A county park, so the long-stay tests are not applied; for review only.
Sites count 61 (derived from older note prose: 37 modern + 24 primitive) left alone; the county page gives 37 modern and 'a variety of primitive campsites' with no number.
Fees: stored $25 electric (primitive $15) confirmed on the fees page, so the group is unchanged. Whether a 23-ft motorhome fits the $15 primitive sites is not stated.
